# Upstream vectors

Authoritative test vectors, transcribed from their published sources. These are
the **only** values in the test suite that prove agreement with something
outside this repository — everything under `crates/*/tests/snapshots/` is a
regression baseline generated by our own code and proves self-consistency only
(DESIGN.md §6).

They must never be edited to make a test pass. A failure here means our code is
wrong, or the transcription is.

| file | source |
|---|---|
| `ed25519.json` | RFC 8032 §7.1, TEST 1–3 |
| `hmac_sha256.json` | RFC 4231 §4.2–4.4, test cases 1–3 |
| `sha512.json` | NIST FIPS 180-4 examples, plus the empty-string digest |

## What is *not* covered here, and why

XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox, NaCl `crypto_box`, AES-256-GCM and Argon2id have
no first-party vectors in this directory yet. They are covered by:

* their own crates' upstream vector suites (`crypto_secretbox`, `crypto_box`,
  `aes-gcm`, `argon2` each ship the published vectors and run them in CI); and
* round-trip property tests in this repository.

That is weaker than a transcribed vector, because it does not independently
check that *we* drive those crates correctly — only that the crates are correct
and that our encrypt and decrypt agree with each other. Closing that gap is
tracked as follow-up work; it does not block M1, because the framing those
primitives sit inside is heylogin's rather than the library's, and the framing
is what M2 confirms.
